columns.text: Keep credentials out of shared files

content.text: A practical guide to running, changing, validating, and deploying the NowTech Admin dashboard.

stack.text:
1. Copy .env.example to .env
2. Add the required local values
3. Run bun install
4. Run bun run dev:local
5. Open http://localhost:3000
Bun, with bun.lock as the only lockfile

content.text: This is a working guide, not a replacement for AGENTS.md. Read that file before changing code. Updated 6 October 2026 for the stock-status controls and the backend repository.

NowTech Admin is the internal operations dashboard for NowTech. It is a Nuxt 4 application that server-renders pages and exposes a Nitro backend-for-frontend (BFF). The browser talks to the admin; the admin owns the authenticated calls to the NowTech backend and Supabase.

columns.text:
Browser
Operators use the English or French UI. The locale cookie is NT-LANG.

Nuxt Admin + BFF
Pages in app/; browser-facing handlers in server/api/.

NowTech backend + Supabase
Domain APIs, catalogue media, and production authentication.

body.text: Nuxt pages, components, composables, plugins, schemas, stores, and browser UI.
Nitro-only authentication, BFF proxy routes, startup checks, and integrations.
Types and helpers shared by app and server.
Modular English and French translation domains.
Flat unit and Nuxt component specs. The include globs are not recursive.

text.text: Never move backend tokens into browser code.

text: Supabase access is created per request in server/utils/supabase.ts, and the sealed session accepts only its cookie. The BFF deliberately allowlists forwarded headers.

ul: Bun. CI uses Bun 1.4.0; use a compatible local version.
The extracted project archive and the configuration values supplied by the handoff team.
A reachable NowTech backend for useful local data and sign-in.
A local .env file. Keep it private and outside shared archives.

body.text:
cd <extracted-project-folder>
cp .env.example .env
bun install
bun run dev:local

content.text: bun install runs Nuxt prepare through postinstall, which creates .nuxt/. Do not use npm, pnpm, or yarn here, even though the older root README lists them.

body.text: At least 32 characters. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. The server will not start with a shorter value.
Supabase endpoint and public anonymous key used by the production-auth path. Use team-provided values.
Backend origin, without /v1. For example, a local backend may be http://localhost:3001.
Convenience source used by .env.example; NUXT_API_BASE_URL references it there.

content.text: Secret rule: .env and .env.* are ignored except for .env.example and the fake-host .env.test. Never commit a copied or real credential file.

The admin does not bundle the business backend; it lives in its own repository, described at the end of this section. This handbook assumes you already have a running API and valid local operator credentials. Installing the backend, PostgreSQL, and fixtures is covered by the backend's own guide.
Point the BFF at the API
Then start the dashboard with bun run dev:local and visit http://localhost:3000. Use the local operator account at the login page.

ol: In non-production only, the admin sends the login email and motDePasse to POST /v1/auth/connexion on NUXT_API_BASE_URL.
The application stores a sealed session cookie, not a browser-exposed backend token.
When NODE_ENV is production, the bypass is unavailable and Supabase authentication is used.

stack.text: Run dev:local for the local backend

bun run dev:local starts the dashboard on port 3000 and clears any BACKEND_URL or NUXT_API_BASE_URL exported in your shell, so the values in .env, which point at your local backend, are the ones used. Plain bun run dev lets a variable left in your shell override .env, and the app may call a different backend.

body.text: Public storefront origin used by product links. It is browser-visible.
Optional logo previews. Only a publishable pk_ key belongs here, never a Logo.dev sk_ secret.
Server-only AI product-copy key. Optional for local work that does not use generation; required in production.
Optional browser-visible support address for the login page.

content.text: The backend is the NowTech-backend- repository. It is edited alongside this app and is no longer treated as read-only. Its guide, documents/travailler-et-deployer.md (written in French), covers local setup, tests, and deployment. These rules matter when an admin change needs a backend change:

body.text: Never push directly to main. Work on a branch and open a pull request that says what changes and why.

Merging into main is the whole release: GitHub notifies Coolify, which rebuilds the image and swaps the container, so the change is live in about two minutes. On every pull request GitHub runs typing, the migrations on a fresh database, the sql/ files applied twice, and the full suite. Do not merge a red one.

Prisma migrations run on a database that already holds orders and money. Write them to pass on production as it is (add column if not exists): a failing migration stops the container from starting. Files in sql/ must be safe to re-run.

In the backend repository, pnpm dev:jeton signs a team token for the administration routes without Supabase. With SUPABASE_URL empty, the backend's own pnpm dev:local turns MOT_DE_PASSE_DEV into every address's password, and a member of boutique.membres_equipe gets their roles.

content.text: Run the smallest useful check first. Before sharing or deploying a change, run the relevant local checks.

body.text: Start the development server at http://localhost:3000, against the backend set in .env.
Plain nuxt dev, without the shell clean-up: a BACKEND_URL or NUXT_API_BASE_URL already exported in your shell overrides .env.

bun run build
bun run preview
Build the SSR app and serve the production output locally.

Run both Vitest projects once. Use bun run test:unit or bun run test:nuxt for a project. The config pins the Nuxt Image settings, so image or Supabase variables in your shell cannot change the result.

bun run format
bun run format:check
Write or verify formatting with oxfmt. Do not hand-format around it.
Check English/French key parity and raw UI strings.
Audit changed code. Always use bunx fallow or the Bun scripts, never a global fallow binary.

stack.text: Run lint, format:check, i18n:check, fallow, typecheck, tests, and build as appropriate for the change.
Set up your own CI and review policy to mirror the local checks. This handoff leaves automation ownership to the new team.

content.text: TDD is the default: for a function, component, or business rule, write a meaningful failing test first, then make it pass. Do not add coverage-only, snapshot-only, or framework tests.

stack.text: bunx vitest run currently reports 12 failing tests in six files: the four ai-product-copy specs, overview-date-field, and products-detail-form. bun run typecheck reports one error, in ai-product-copy-service. All of them predate the stock-status work and are recorded in reports/2026-10-05-assessment-vitest-failures.md and reports/2026-10-05-assessment-typecheck-failure.md. A few heavy Nuxt specs can also time out when the whole suite runs under load; rerun the file on its own before treating it as a regression.

body.text: Use TanStack Query. Pinia is for browser-only state such as preferences and draft filters, not a mirror of API data.
Create one folder per component. Do not edit app/components/ui/ unless the user explicitly asks; it is generated shadcn-vue output.
Use NuxtLinkLocale for internal links and custom localized routes. Small, stable components may use per-component messages.
Use Tailwind utilities and existing CSS tokens. Tailwind is configured in app/assets/css/main.css, not a tailwind.config file.
Unit specs are Node; components use Nuxt + happy-dom. Keep files directly in test/unit or test/nuxt because the globs are flat.

content.text: A plan, implementation, and review share one kebab-case slug. Plans go in plans/, implementation walkthroughs in walkthroughs/, and reviews in reviews/. Investigations without a plan go in reports/.
Keep each change narrow, explain its validation, and preserve other contributors' work.

Two things describe a product's stock: the quantity counted, and whether the shop sells it. Since 6 October they are separate. The Overview tab puts the delivery time first and the two controls below it, side by side; the Stock tab holds the count and its movements.

body.text: The selling status. Out of stock hides the product from the storefront and makes new carts refuse it. While a product tracks its quantity the switch is locked, because the count decides.

On means the product is counted and follows its count. Turning it off keeps today's status as an explicit decision, so customers see no change; turning it on hands the decision back to the count. A product that was never counted cannot be tracked until you count it with the pencil beside the quantity.
Names who decides: Follows the count, From WooCommerce, or Set in the panel. The last one is shown in a warning tone because a panel decision overrides every WooCommerce import.
Marks a product that has never been counted. Its quantity reads 0, muted.
A warning dialog quotes the count, for example when hiding a product that has 7 in stock. Nothing is written until staff confirm.

A button on the Stock tab, offered only for an uncounted product whose status was set in the panel. Its dialog names the status being dropped; Confirm clears the decision, so the shop uses WooCommerce's status again, now and after every import. A counted product hands the decision back with Track quantity instead.
The quantity starts empty. Leave it empty to sell without counting, and pick a Status (In stock by default); enter a quantity to count the product and let the quantity decide.

An Out of stock set in the panel hides the product and refuses new carts, but staff can still confirm an order the customer placed earlier. A product that is out of stock because its count is zero, or whose count cannot cover the order, still blocks the confirmation.
Hidden for a product that was never counted, and while a panel decision is in force.

stack.text: The decision lives in its own table, boutique.produit_disponibilites, and is written by PATCH /v1/catalogue/administration/produits/:id/disponibilite. The call is direction-only, never creates a stock row or a movement, and is journalled as stock.disponibilite_modifiee. The table sits outside what the WooCommerce ingestion replaces, so a decision survives a re-ingestion.

content.text: These constraints are deliberate. Treat them as design boundaries, not cleanup opportunities.

body.text: nuxt-zod-i18n depends on zod 3 runtime exports. Zod 4 causes a Nitro production import failure.
vue-tsc 3 resolves a TypeScript path that TypeScript 7 no longer exports.
A singleton can retain a session in memory and leak one request's context to another.
It prevents an x-nt-session header from bypassing the cookie-only session boundary.
proxyRequest would forward the sealed Cookie by default. The explicit proxy headers protect that boundary.
The shared backend throttler is 10 requests per second. A six-query SSR dashboard is a design error.
French backend details remain beneath translated status headlines because the backend does not yet supply stable error codes.
Set status through the decision, not the count
Never write a movement or a stock row just to flip a status. Use the disponibilite endpoint, so the register keeps recording counts only.
Write translation keys as literal t() calls
scripts/check-translation-keys.mjs, run by i18n:check, cannot verify a key built from a template string.

stack.text: nuxt-security disables its XSS validator only below /api/** because it can rewrite valid JSON values. Backend validation remains the input boundary. Do not broaden that exception.

content.text: If an instruction seems unexpected, find its rationale in AGENTS.md or the linked postmortems before changing it.
This is an SSR Nitro application. Do not treat nuxt generate as the normal production deployment path.

body.text:
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run build
node .output/server/index.mjs

content.text: For a local smoke check after building, run bun run preview. Nitro honours PORT or NITRO_PORT and HOST or NITRO_HOST when serving the output.

ul: Set the required session, Supabase, API-origin, catalogue-image, and storefront values from the environment section.
Set NUXT_OPENAI_API_KEY when deploying. The startup configuration check requires it in production, even when local development can omit it.
Keep every secret server-only. Public NUXT_PUBLIC_* values are intentionally exposed to the browser.
Set NUXT_BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET when the backend is configured to recognise this server's requests outside its normal shared rate limit.
Do not depend on NUXT_LOCAL_AUTH_BYPASS in production. The code blocks it when NODE_ENV is production.

stack.text: The handoff materials do not establish a hosting project, deployment workflow, domain configuration, approval path, or rollback procedure. Agree these operational details with the new owning team before releasing. Do not invent them.

content.text: Confirm the build succeeds, the deployed environment has every required secret, the target backend origin is correct, and the deployment owner has a rollback path. Keep the AI product-copy model and its matching input/output cost values aligned before relying on audit cost figures.
The backend ships on its own: a merge into its main branch deploys it. When an admin change calls a new backend endpoint, as the stock-status controls do, the backend change must be live first.
Use the handbook to get productive, then use the source of truth for the detail.
